body.text: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights and the Responsibilities of United Nations Member States
Written by: Sardar Nasir Aziz Khan

The beauty of our world lies in its diversity. We the people of Jammu Kashmir are a beautiful combination of different religions, ethnicities, cultures, and languages, and this is the reality of almost every country in the world. There is hardly any country where people belonging to only one religion, belief, or language reside. The historical State of Jammu and Kashmir is no different. It is a land enriched with a multi-religious, multi-ethnic, and multilingual heritage.

If other diverse nations can live together as one nation in peace and harmony, why are the people of Jammu and Kashmir not being given the right to do the same? Why are they told that people who speak different languages and belong to different regions cannot live together? Those who make such claims are certainly neither well-wishers of the State of Jammu and Kashmir nor do they have any sympathy for Kashmiris.

In India, people belonging to different religions and speaking hundreds of languages, the majority of whom do not speak Hindi, can be Indian. In Pakistan, people belonging to different religions and speaking dozens of different languages, the majority of whom do not speak Urdu, can be Pakistani.

However, when it comes to the State of Jammu and Kashmir, the occupying powers and their stooges promote hatred, hostility, and extremism on regional, linguistic, religious, and ideological grounds. They argue that the people of Jammu speak Dogri, so how can they live together with the Kashmiri-speaking people of Srinagar? How can the people of Ladakh live together with Dogri and Kashmiri speakers?

Similarly, the same malicious propaganda is spread about Gilgit-Baltistan, so-called Azad Kashmir, and other constituent regions of the State of Jammu and Kashmir. Some so-called individuals who describe themselves as nationalists and freedom advocates are also advancing the propaganda of the occupying powers, without feeling the slightest regret or shame.

Those who are engaged in increasing hatred among the inhabitants of different constituent regions of the State of Jammu and Kashmir are, in fact, serving the interests  of the occupying powers. They have no interest in the rights and freedom of the people of Jammu and Kashmir. Effective and serious measures are needed to monitor such elements and defeat their malicious intentions.

To identify such elements, adopt a simple principle: anyone who spreads hatred and prejudice among the people of the State of Jammu and Kashmir is not a well-wisher of Kashmiris. Whether that person belongs to your family, your tribe, disguises themselves as a nationalist, is a religious leader, claims to be an intellectual, presents themselves as a political leader, wears the cloak of a journalist, or appears in any other form, that person is nothing more than an agent of the occupying powers.
It is a reality that there is hardly any country in the world where human rights violations do not occur. However, understanding the nature and severity of these violations is extremely important.

The forced division of the State of Jammu and Kashmir is a bitter reality. The Kashmir issue is not merely a bilateral , territorial or regional dispute. It is a question of the lives and survival of millions of Kashmiris. Its resolution is possible only in accordance with the wishes and will of the Kashmiri people.
Any kind of unilateral or imposed decisions are making this issue increasingly complicated and dangerous, potentially leading to a nuclear war at any time.

For resolving such disputes, valuable guidance can be drawn from the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR), adopted in 1948. This declaration represents a milestone and serves as a universal charter for establishing the fundamental rights of all human beings.

It calls for every human being to be treated with equality, dignity, and respect. The UDHR is founded on the pillars of freedom, equality, and fraternity, and every article of this declaration is extremely important.

It contains numerous articles directly relevant to the situation in Jammu and Kashmir. This declaration is not merely a list of ideas but an excellent framework for accountability and action, the implementation of which is obligatory upon every member state of the United Nations.
Important Articles of the Declaration and Jammu and Kashmir
Article 1: This article forms the foundation of the entire declaration:
"All human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights."

This article is a powerful declaration against every form of discrimination or forced division. It emphasizes our shared humanity, which transcends all prejudices based on religion, race, country, region, gender, language, and belief.

In this context, the forced division of the State of Jammu and Kashmir and its people, religious hatred and prejudice, and every action that divides people into families, regions, and communities are contrary to the fundamental principles of this universal declaration.
Article 2: This article further reinforces that every person is entitled to all the rights and freedoms set forth in the declaration "without distinction of any kind."

This presents a direct challenge to the situation in Jammu and Kashmir, where people are deprived of their fundamental human rights on the basis of their ethnicity, beliefs, region, identity, language, and political affiliation.
The rights described in the declaration must apply equally to all people. No country, region, or place is entitled to any exception.
Article 3: This article guarantees the right to life, liberty, and personal security.
The prolonged conflict, forced division, and forced displacement continuing in Jammu and Kashmir are direct violations of this right.
For several decades, people in the region have been living under oppression, violence, and fear. Millions have been forced to leave their homes and seek refuge in other countries.
The right to live in peace and security is a fundamental human right that must be restored throughout all parts of the State of Jammu and Kashmir.
Article 4: This article states:
"No one shall be held in slavery or servitude."
Slavery and the slave trade shall be prohibited in all their forms.
Article 5: According to this article:
"No one shall be subjected to torture or to cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment."
Enforced disappearances, custodial torture, extrajudicial killings, and inhuman treatment are clear violations of this article.
Article 6: According to this article:
"Everyone has the right to recognition everywhere as a person before the law."
Article 7: This article states:
"All are equal before the law and are entitled without any discrimination to equal protection of the law."
Discrimination based on religion, ethnicity, language, or political affiliation is contrary to this article.
Article 8: According to this article:
"Everyone has the right to an effective legal remedy against acts violating their fundamental rights."
The absence of an independent judicial system and the lack of access to justice undermine this right.
Article 9: This article states:
"No one shall be subjected to arbitrary arrest, detention or exile."
Detaining any individual without trial or forcing them into exile constitutes a violation of this article.
Article 10: According to this article:
"Everyone is entitled in full equality to a fair and public hearing by an independent and impartial tribunal."
Interference by influential institutions and individuals in the judicial system undermines this fundamental right.
Article 13: This article is particularly important for the people of Jammu and Kashmir.
It states:
"Everyone has the right to freedom of movement and residence within the borders of their country or state."
It also guarantees the full right to leave one's country, settle in another country, and return to one's own country.
For the past eight decades, the people of the historical State of Jammu and Kashmir have suffered from forced division.
They are not freely permitted to meet their families across the so-called Line of Control or visit their ancestral homes.
These oppressive restrictions on their freedom of movement constitute a direct violation of their human rights.

In Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan, human rights representatives, nationalist leaders, and pro-independence political leaders have been placed under Schedule IV, meaning they cannot travel freely from one place to another.
To travel from one area to another, they are required to obtain permission from the police and administrative authorities.
Similarly, blocking travel documents, creating obstacles to obtaining them, and cancelling or confiscating such documents are contrary to the universal charter.
The immediate abolition of such discriminatory laws and regulations is essential.
Article 16: This article guarantees the right to marry and establish a family.
As a result of the forced division of the State of Jammu and Kashmir, countless families have been separated.
Restrictions on people's freedom of movement have made it extremely difficult for families to meet one another and maintain their relationships.

The right to choose a life partner and establish a family is a fundamental human right. However, forced division has deprived a large number of people in the region of this right, placing their culture, language, family values, and identity under serious threat.
Articles 18, 19, and 20: These articles guarantee freedom of thought, conscience, religion, expression, ideological opinion, peaceful assembly, association, freedom of the press, and other rights.
These rights are extremely important for democratic processes and for ensuring that all voices are heard.
In Jammu and Kashmir, these rights have frequently been suppressed.

For example, in Azad Kashmir, mobile services and the internet have remained shut down for more than four months, from 5 June 2026 until the present, in an effort to suppress the peoples  rights movement.

According to international media reports, approximately one hundred people have been martyred, hundreds have been forcibly disappeared, and thousands have been arrested without being presented before any competent court.
This means they are being deprived of the rights guaranteed to them under international law and the Universal Charter of Human Rights.
Taking human lives through extrajudicial killings constitutes the commission of serious crimes against humanity.
An insulting and inflammatory campaign against Kashmiris is being conducted in the media by federal ministers and certain journalists, and Kashmiris are facing discriminatory treatment.
Pro-independence and nationalist leaders are prevented from participating in elections, and nationalist political parties are not registered with the Election Commission.

In Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan, political and human rights leaders face restrictions on their freedom of movement and have been placed on Schedule IV lists, severely limiting their political activities.

These restrictions on fundamental freedoms prevent local people, political leaders, and social and human rights representatives from advocating for the rights of their people and make it impossible for them to participate fully in democratic processes and political life.
Article 21: This article grants everyone the right to participate in the government of their country, either directly or through freely chosen representatives.
Restrictions on political participation and the absence of genuine self-determination in the region are direct violations of this article.
The people of Jammu and Kashmir have the right to determine their own future and express their views on decisions that affect their lives.
In Indian-administered Jammu and Kashmir, the special status of the state was unilaterally abolished on 5 August 2019.

A resolution was passed in the Jammu and Kashmir Assembly demanding the restoration of Jammu and Kashmir's statehood and special status. However, this resolution has not yet been considered by the Indian government.
Such actions are contrary to the Universal Charter of Human Rights.

Protecting the rights of local people, their demands, aspirations, and fundamental human rights is among the primary responsibilities of the state, and these obligations apply to every member state of the United Nations.
Peace, Dialogue, and the Responsibilities of the Parties
We believe that war can never be the solution to any problem. War only brings destruction, devastation, and an increase in the number of graves in cemeteries.
History has repeatedly demonstrated that all conflicts, whether world wars or recent disputes, are ultimately resolved through negotiations and dialogue.
This is the only path to lasting peace in Jammu and Kashmir.

We call upon the Government of Pakistan to abandon its policy of suppressing people  rights movements through the use of force, immediately initiate negotiations with the Joint Awami Action Committee, and implement in full and exactly as agreed the agreement concluded with the Joint Awami Action Committee on 4 October 2025.
We also wish to tell the Awami Action Committee that the refugees of the State of Jammu and Kashmir are joint inheritors of this region.
They must be granted representation in the Assembly in proportion to their population, according to the same principle under which Assembly constituencies have been established in Azad Kashmir.

Allowing non-state residents to contest elections for seats reserved for Kashmiri refugees through fake domicile certificates and fraudulent documents, and granting them employment in Azad Kashmir on the basis of forged documents, constitutes a serious violation of United Nations resolutions concerning Jammu and Kashmir and international law.

The State Subject Rule of Jammu and Kashmir is being systematically violated in Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan to alter the demographic composition of these regions, undermine the rights of the indigenous population, and facilitate demographic changes.
People in Indian-administered Jammu, Kashmir, and Ladakh are engaged in widespread protests.

Through the illegal and unilateral action of 5 August 2019, Articles 370 and 35-A of the Indian Constitution were effectively abrogated, and the historical State of Jammu and Kashmir was divided into two Union Territories.

Under the pretext of development and the promotion of tourism, domicile certificates and other official documents are being issued to non-state residents, facilitating changes to the demographic composition of the region.
People in Ladakh, Jammu, and Kashmir are protesting, yet serious violations of international law and United Nations resolutions by the government continue unabated.
The exploitation of the inhabitants of the State of Jammu and Kashmir through military power, force, and majoritarian dominance continues on both sides of the so-called Line of Control.
Recent developments have once again drawn the attention of the international community toward the State of Jammu and Kashmir.
These developments include the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights expressing deep concern and issuing a statement regarding the situation in Azad Kashmir.
They also include the spokesperson for the United Nations Secretary-General stating that "United Nations resolutions on Kashmir still remain in their original form."

Furthermore, the United Nations updating the world map and showing the entire State of Jammu and Kashmir, as it existed until 22 October 1947, as a disputed state sends a clear message that unilateral decisions imposed by India and Pakistan through force cannot change historical facts.

The fragmentation of the State of Jammu and Kashmir, the annexation of its territories, and their further division are not only unacceptable to all constituent regions of the State of Jammu and Kashmir, but the United Nations and the international community are also closely monitoring such actions.

More than 80 members of the British Parliament writing a letter to the United Nations Secretary-General, demanding attention to human rights violations in Azad Kashmir and occupied Jammu and Kashmir, supporting the Kashmiris' right to self-determination, and calling for a resolution of the Kashmir issue in accordance with United Nations resolutions reflect the fact that the sacrifices of Kashmiris have not been in vain.
Forced division, medieval laws, and inhuman atrocities cannot prevent Kashmiris from reaching their destination.
A Sustainable Solution and the Future Course of Action
We believe that India and Pakistan must come to their senses and take concrete measures based on human rights principles to achieve a peaceful and lasting resolution of the Kashmir issue.
These measures should include the following:
- The rights of the Kashmiri people must be fully respected.
- Freedom of movement must be restored, allowing them to travel freely across the Line of Control and return to their ancestral homes.
- All citizens, including pro-independence and nationalist leaders, must be allowed to participate freely in elections and political processes.
- Family reunification must be ensured so that divided families can meet one another and live together.
- All citizens must have equal access to education, healthcare, and employment.

- The inhabitants of the entire State of Jammu and Kashmir must be allowed freedom of movement. In the first phase, the State of Jammu and Kashmir should be established as a buffer state, maintaining friendly relations with all its neighbouring countries.
Through these measures and respect for fundamental rights, we can create an environment where peace, prosperity, and peaceful coexistence are not merely ideas but a reality.

The resolution of this longstanding dispute will not only end human rights violations and suffering in Jammu and Kashmir but will also usher in a new era of development and stability for all regions of South Asia.
The time has come to put down the guns and embrace dialogue, dignity, and the principles of human rights.

If India and Pakistan fail to take immediate and serious measures and do not grant Kashmiris their fundamental human rights, they must not forget that global powers have been closely watching this region for a long time.
The entire State of Jammu and Kashmir holds immense geographical, regional, economic, and strategic defence importance.
Global powers possess large armies, advanced weapons, and tremendous economic strength, which could alter the geography and balance of the entire South Asian region at any time.
